messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@greenleaf.io>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: billing@greenleaf.io
Date: Tue, 04 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discrepancy in Oct marketplace payout / withheld allocation

Hi Tessa / Jonas,

We just received the October AWS Marketplace settlement and noticed ~USD 48,200 is listed as 'withheld - pending reconciliation' on your statement. Our internal invoice (attached) shows the same consumption but the allocation to our entity ID (GLF-US-01) does not match the usage lines you provided through the marketplace (split across two merchant IDs).

Can you confirm:
- Why the marketplace settlement shows a different merchant attribution for ~1,200 usage records?
- Whether Redwood will issue a credit memo for the withheld amount or re-route payout to the correct entity?

This is blocking our finance close; if you can triage this week that'd be ideal. I attached the PDF invoice and a CSV extract of our internal mapping.

Thanks,
Samantha Ortiz
Director, Finance Operations | GreenLeaf Analytics
Samantha Ortiz | billing@greenleaf.io

Attachment: GreenLeaf_AWS_invoice_Oct2025.pdf (PDF, 420KB)
Attachment: GLF-usage-export-202510.csv (CSV, 1.1MB)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com

Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 04 Nov 2025 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in Oct marketplace payout / withheld allocation

Samantha — thanks for the heads-up and for the attachments. We're looking into this. High-level plan:

1) Internal rolodex: Jonas will pull the marketplace ingestion logs and crosswalk the merchant IDs to Redwood's merchant routing table.
2) Recompute: we'll run a short reconciliation pass to determine which usage lines were misattributed and whether the hold is from a marketplace split or our onboarding mapping.
3) Outcome: either (a) issue a credit memo for the withheld amount against Oct settlement, or (b) re-route the pending payout to the GLF-US-01 merchant if marketplace records support that.

Can you confirm the legal entity your finance team expects payment to land in (bank/account name) so we can prepare the credit memo or payout reroute? Also, please confirm whether GreenLeaf accepts a credit memo now and a net-settlement in December, or if you need a direct transfer.

I'll keep you posted by EOD Thursday.

—Tessa Morgan
Revenue Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-credit-memo-GLF-20251108.pdf (stub)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 05 Nov 2025 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in Oct marketplace payout / withheld allocation

Quick update from the logs: I pulled the GCP & AWS ingestion feeds and matched the usage rows to our merchant routing table. Findings so far:

- ~1,180 lines (corresponding to ~USD 46,900) were ingested with a legacy merchant_id (mch-GLF-legacy) that should have been rewritten to mch-GLF-US-01 during the onboarding normalization step, but the ORION_TRANSFORMER job failed on Oct 29 for that partition.
- The failure produced a partial retry that duplicated some usage rows under the fallback merchant (mch-GLF-eu), which is why the marketplace settlement shows split attribution.
- The raw marketplace manifests (attached to the Drive link) show the correct original merchant tags; the issue is our post-ingest rewrite.

Proposed remediation:
- Retro-run the normalization on the affected partition, de-dupe the duplicated rows, and produce a corrected ledger.
- Generate a credit memo for the net amount of duplicated + misattributed usage (estimate attached).
- We should also submit an evidence bundle to AWS Marketplace Support to request re-payout where possible.

I'll start the recalculation now; ETA for a clean ledger is tomorrow EOD. I added a short export to the shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/billing/GLF/oct-metering-logs (sample manifest + error trace).

—Jonas
Principal, Marketplace Integrations | Redwood Inference

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@greenleaf.io>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, aws-marketplace-support@amazon.com
Date: Fri, 08 Nov 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Resolved: proposed credit and next steps for Oct settlement (GreenLeaf)

Samantha — quick update and next steps now that we've reconciled the ledger. TL;DR: we identified the ingestion normalization failure as the root cause, removed the duplicated rows, and are proposing a credit memo to clear the withheld amount.

What we did:
- Re-ran normalization for the affected partition (Oct 26–30) and de-duped 1,197 rows. Net amount attributable to misrouting: USD 48,120.
- Generated a proposed credit memo (attached) and prepared a short evidence bundle for AWS Marketplace (manifest + error traces).
- Opened a support request with AWS (ref: 112233-aws-marketplace-GLF) to request a reallocation where their settlement supports it — if AWS accepts the evidence, they can re-route payout to the GLF-US-01 merchant. If not, Redwood will issue the credit memo to GreenLeaf to reconcile the withheld balance.

Requested confirmation from GreenLeaf:
1) Please confirm the payee entity for the credit memo (legal name + billing email).
2) Do you prefer a netted credit on your next settlement (Dec) or an immediate direct transfer to your bank? If direct transfer, please provide wire details or a signed remittance form.

Next steps (our side):
- If you confirm payee & accept credit memo: we will issue the credit and apply to your Dec settlement.
- If you ask for direct transfer: we'll coordinate a one-time payout and share the remittance documentation.
- We'll keep AWS support looped until their decision is final (we expect 7–10 business days).

Attachments: proposed-credit-memo-GLF-20251108.pdf (PDF, stub)
Support ticket: https://aws.amazon.com/support/cases/112233-aws-marketplace-GLF

Apologies for the operational friction — we're putting a postmortem action item on the ingestion pipeline (ORION_TRANSFORMER) to add retries and an alert on rewrite failures so this doesn't recur.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Revenue Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0192
